newsitem.title: BRAZIL: North Brazil sugar ports not hit by strike yet.
newsitem.headline: North Brazil sugar ports not hit by strike yet.

text.p: Stevedores at Brazil's two sugar ports in the north-northeast region are either not going to join or have still to decide if they will join a national strike which was to have begun at 0700 local/1000 GMT today, officials said.
In Recife, the key sugar port, local union secretary Mario Ferreira said members had decided not to take part in the 48-hour stoppage.
Earlier this week, Ferreira had said Recife workers may carry on working because of a clause in a recently-negotiated contract with the port authority which ruled out strikes without due cause.

In Maceio, there were no vessels currently docked at the port and stevedores were to hold an assembly only this evening to see if they would go on strike as of Saturday, a port authority official said.
However, any stoppage would not hit sugar as the only vessels expected Saturday were a wheat and a fertilizer vessel, he added.

The national strike was called in sympathy with workers at Santos who began an indefinite stoppage as of April 15 to protest a local steel firm using its own workers at its private terminal at the port.
Fresh talks betweeen the steel firm and union representatives are scheduled to begin at 0900 today, a federation official said.
